'''Rassolnik''' ({{langx|ru|рассольник}} {{IPA|ru|rɐˈs(ː)olʲnʲɪk|}}) is a traditional [[Russian cuisine|Russian]] soup made from [[pickled cucumber]]s, [[pearl barley]], and pork or beef [[Kidney#As food|kidneys]].<ref name="Goldstein">{{cite book | author=Darra Goldstein | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aKEICug2T-EC&pg=PA53 | title=A Taste of Russia: A Cookbook of Russian Hospitality | publisher=Russian Information Service | year=1999 | isbn=9781880100424 | pages=53}}</ref> A vegetarian variant of rassolnik also exists, usually made during [[Lent]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Постный рассольник |url=http://cookberry.net/recipe/vegan-rassolnik/ |access-date=2022-04-15 |website=Cookberry |language=ru-RU |archive-date=2022-08-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817070027/http://cookberry.net/recipe/vegan-rassolnik/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The dish is known to have existed as far back as the 15th century, when it was called ''kalya''. Rassolnik became part of the common [[Soviet cuisine]] and today it is also popular in [[Ukrainian cuisine|Ukraine]] (as ''rozsoljnyk'') and [[Belarusian cuisine|Belarus]] (as ''rasoljnik'').<ref>Українські страви. К.:Державне видавництво технічної літератури УРСР. 1961. 454 с.</ref> A similar dish is common in [[Poland]], where it is known as ''[[zupa ogórkowa]]'' (literally 'cucumber soup').

The key part of rassolnik is the ''[[brine (food)|rassol]]'', a liquid based on the juice of pickled cucumbers with various other seasonings. It is a favourite [[hangover]] remedy.<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ePHkDwAAQBAJ&pg=PT26|title=Mamushka: A Cookbook |author=Olia Hercules|chapter=Rassol`nyk|publisher=WeldonOwn+ORM|year=2015|isbn=978-1681880747}}</ref>
